subject: Purchase options: AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace vs direct vendor invoice — questions from Aperture Health
messages:
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@aperturehealth.com>

Cc: Aperture Health Purchasing <procure@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood purchase path questions for EU pilot

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Aperture's procurement team asked me to capture a few specifics so they can decide whether to route our planned EU pilot through an AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace private offer or via a direct Redwood invoice under an MSA. High-level items they need answered:

- Can we get directed invoicing to our EU entity if we go through the marketplace private offer?
- How are co-sell credits handled if we list in the marketplace vs direct deal? Any revenue-share implications?
- For a regulated healthcare pilot we need EU data residency and SOC2 evidence — are those treated any differently by route?
- Procurement timeline: marketplace private offers sometimes accelerate purchasing approvals because they show up in the vendor portal. Is that true here?

I'm attaching our RFP and a short procurement checklist. Would like a short writeup we can give procurement and legal so they can pick a lane. Can you also confirm any differences in lead times for PO issuance / invoice processing?

Best,
Eleanor

Subject: Re: Redwood purchase path questions for EU pilot

Hi Eleanor — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the RFP. I've summarized the pragmatic differences below and attached a short checklist that procurement/legal can use during their intake review.

Marketplace private offer (AWS/Azure/GCP)
- Invoicing: Many marketplaces support "directed invoices" to a specific buyer entity via private offers, but exact seller-of-record and tax handling depends on the cloud provider and your entity's configuration. We can generally route invoices to your EU legal entity when using a private offer—we'll work with the marketplace team to ensure correct SOR settings.
- Procurement speed: Private offers often shorten procurement approval when buyers use their cloud procurement portal (PO + automatic acceptance flows).
- Co-sell: Listing can unlock cloud co-sell/go-to-market programs; co-sell credits are tracked by the marketplace and aggregated differently than our direct deals. If you need credits applied to your internal partner incentives, we should confirm mapping early.
- Compliance/data residency: No change to the product — data residency/SOC2 are controls independent of purchase lane; the routing does not change where data is processed if you select an EU region deployment. We'll provide the SOC2 report and data residency matrix regardless of the purchase route.

Direct vendor invoice (MSA + Redwood invoice)
- Invoicing: Redwood invoices directly to the entity you specify; this is the simplest path if your AP team requires our invoice to go to an EU tax ID we control.
- Procurement speed: Can be slower if legal needs to negotiate MSAs/terms; however, for pilots we often offer a short-form MSA and SOW to speed this up.
- Co-sell: Direct deals make co-sell attribution manual (we can provide the partner/co-sell paperwork), and you may lose certain marketplace-driven incentives.

Recommendation and next steps
- For a first pilot where AP wants a fast PO/portal visibility: marketplace private offer is often faster, provided we confirm directed-invoice capability for your EU entity.
- If your AP requires Redwood to be the seller-of-record with an EU tax ID on the invoice, choose direct vendor invoice; we can accelerate with a short MSA + SOW and pre-populated invoice templates.

I've attached: Redwood_Marketplace_vs_Direct_Checklist.xlsx (procurement-ready checklist) and a one-pager.

If useful, we can run a 30-min call with procurement + our billing ops next week to validate the invoice flow for the specific cloud provider you prefer (EAST EU vs. other regions). What days/times work?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Redwood purchase path questions for EU pilot — suggested sales guidance

Naomi — forwarding suggested guidance for the team and a recommended commercial approach.

Notes for Sales/Finance ops:
- If Aperture wants the fastest procurement path and are open to marketplace billing, prioritize an AWS/Azure private offer and confirm directed-invoice to their EU entity before listing. Ask legal to confirm taxes/SOR.
- If Aperture insists on Redwood issuing the invoice to an EU tax ID (vendor invoice), propose: short-form MSA + 3-month pilot SOW; offer a 12% pilot discount with right-to-renegotiate on expansion. This avoids lengthy legal redlines and keeps margins protected.
- Co-sell credit: If they list on the marketplace, we'll rely on provider attribution; for direct deals we will fill out the cloud co-sell nomination paperwork so partner credits can be applied — but timing differs.

Can someone from finance ops prepare both a private-offer draft (marketplace) and a short MSA + SOW template so we can present both lanes on the call? I'm OK with a 12% pilot concession for a quick close; escalate anything beyond that.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

If we can get both docs by EOD Wed our AP team will try to get the PO out that week.
